nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-03.prompt: Compute the number of positive integral factors of $1002001$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-04.prompt: $P$ is an interior point in rectangle $ABCD$. $PA = 6$, $PC = 5$, and $PB = 7$. Compute $PD$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-06.prompt: If four fair dice are rolled, compute the probability that the sum is $10$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-08.prompt: Compute the largest possible value of $n$ such that $3^n$ is a factor of $100!$

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-09.prompt: Working alone, Arthur can paint a room in $6$ hours. Working alone, Boris can paint the same room in $8$ hours. If they begin the job together, and Boris takes an hour off for lunch, compute the amount of time it will take for the room to be painted.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-10.prompt: The measures of two sides of a triangle are $12$ and $14$ and the medians drawn to these sides are perpendicular to each other. Compute the length of the third side of the triangle.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-11.prompt: The number $3{,}956{,}427{,}8ab$ is divisible by $72$. Compute the ordered pair $(a, b)$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-12.prompt: Compute the sum of the digits of the first $200$ even natural numbers.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-13.prompt: In a triangle, the measure of whose sides are $8$, $15$, and $17$, a circle is inscribed. Compute the measure of the radius of the circle.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-14.prompt: Compute the number of the first $1000$ natural numbers that are not divisible by either $2$ or $3$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-15.prompt: In a game of softball, the probability of Archie getting a hit in an at-bat is $\frac14$. The probability of Betty getting a hit in an at-bat is $\frac13$. The probability of Veronica getting a hit in an at-bat is $\frac12$. If each of the three goes to bat once in the first inning, compute the probability that exactly one gets a hit.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-16.prompt: In right triangle $ABC$, $AC = 15$, and $C$ is the right angle. If all of the measures of the sides of the triangle are integers, compute all possible ordered pairs $(BC, AB)$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-17.prompt: Consider all positive integers with a left-most digit of $2$. They are written next to each other, in ascending order, to form a number $(2202122\ldots)$. Compute the $2005^{\text{th}}$ digit of this number.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-junior-18.prompt: Compute, to the nearest second, the first time after 3:00 AM that the hands of a clock are perpendicular to each other.
